touches.text: Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged. [Q#90: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?]

What the waker starts outlives whoever started it (detached, or through systemd-run --user, which gives it its own memory cap and log while still deciding nothing). Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke. [Q#92: A proof that starts Windows processes stays red until it has your word (CAIRN_PROOF_MAY_SPAWN=1). Measured 2026-11-12: tooth 2 of dc945eb1f072 (cairn.cmd against Git Bash) is red on exactly that word, and nothing in this outline says what the word is. Is it an env var each run sets, a standing flag in ~/.cairn, or may a proof spawn one short hidden process without asking?]
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
It writes one JSON record at the end of a pass listing each device: beat time, device folder found or NOT FOUND, file mtime, pid spawned. It does no checks and no takeover.

Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
